children.counts: slow duple meter with emphasis on quarter-note hops
children.game_version: simplified hopping in place with call-and-response counting

seniors.tempo_and_range: reduced tempo and smaller hops recommended

movement_profile.footwork: Hopping steps on quarter and eighth notes, mostly in place without advancing or retreating
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Couples in circle or line formation
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Light, springy movement emphasizing vertical lift
movement_profile.partnering: Couples dance together but detailed partnering not described

signature_moves.description: A hopping step used to conclude movements and phrases
signature_moves.name: Pas de Rigaudon

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Brisk and lively with clear duple pulse
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid lateral stepping or advancing during hopping steps; maintain vertical bounce

music_profile.musical_form: Regular eight-measure phrases, often paired movements (Rigaudon I and II)
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Quarter-note upbeat followed by steady quarter and eighth notes creating hopping rhythm
music_profile.sound_description: Bright harpsichord or string textures with a steady, hopping rhythm in duple meter; phrases are regular and balanced, evoking cheerful, lively courtly dance.
music_profile.vocal_style: instrumental dance music, no vocals described

basic_steps: Begin with a quarter-note upbeat hop in place
Perform hopping steps on quarter and eighth notes without advancing
Use the pas de rigaudon to conclude movements
Dance in couples arranged in a circle or line
Maintain vertical bouncing with light footwork
teaching.formation: Couples dancing in circle or line formation
teaching.level_notes: Beginners start with hopping in place to the rhythm; intermediate dancers learn the pas de rigaudon and phrase endings; advanced dancers perform stylized court versions with precise timing.
teaching.rhythm: Lively duple meter (2/2 or 2/4) with regular eight-measure phrases and quarter-note upbeat
